test_title: PYST 27: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - Quant (Held On 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: PQ is the diameter of the circle with center O and R, S, T are three points on the semi-circle in a given figure. Which of the following statements is true?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to Thales' Theorem, the angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of a circle is always 90°.

Since PQ is the diameter and points R, S, and T lie on the semi-circle (circumference), the angles ∠PRQ, ∠PSQ, and ∠PTQ must all be 90°.

From the given options, the statement ∠that PTQ and ∠PRQ are equal to 90° is a fundamental geometric property of the semi-circle.

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** PQ is the diameter of the circle with center O. R, S, T are points on the semi-circle.

**Formula:** Angle in a semi-circle is 90°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b272f93075b255a3829fc8ec1d82eaff46a4f9aee9c91152adbc7b9d15b91c2b.png] 

⇒ In a circle, the angle subtended by an arc at the center is twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the circumference.

⇒ For the diameter PQ, the angle subtended at the center O is a straight angle, i.e., ∠POQ = 180°.

⇒ ∠PTQ = ∠PRQ = (1/2) × ∠POQ

⇒ ∠PTQ = ∠PRQ = (1/2) × 180°

⇒ ∠PTQ = ∠PRQ = 90°

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc or chord at the circumference in the same segment are equal. For example, ∠RPS = ∠RTS if they share arc RS.

Central Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle (Center ∠ = 2 × Circumference ∠).

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral whose all four vertices lie on the circumference of a circle is called cyclic. The sum of its opposite angles is 180°.

Radius and Tangent

A tangent at any point on a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact (Angle = 90°).
